- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 3–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- In low sentiment (≤0.2) environments, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward historical mean.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days show downward drift, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day moving average or 10-day trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.5 → 0.1 → 0.5), model often fails to adjust; apply 1–3% correction toward sentiment shift direction.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day high, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) and volatility is high.
